title: Vegas Part 02
summary: Episode 114 continues the Las Vegas recording for nearly two and a half hours. It moves from gambling relapse and Eva Lin speculation through repeated checks about whether recording is active; Bobby Lee's arrival; Asa's repeated lap-dance refusals; a pressured intimate disclosure from Bill Poon; Critter and Bobby nickname origins; the Barstow trip; David's explicit rejection of the fan nickname `Choey`; a private toy-store customer covertly recorded and narrowed by workplace clues; a claimed casino-scam and arson-plan story; HIV misinformation; and venue filming permission that remains undecided. The audit rejects destructive global edits, preserves every slur, fantasy and contradiction, and separates literal transcript, consent, uncertainty, factual correction and public discovery.
source_notes: The raw file contains 4,592 segments and approximately 26,482 words; the clean file contains 4,584 segments and the same approximate word count across 8,787.70 seconds.
All eight cleaner removals are empty zero-duration artifacts. No spoken idea is removed.
Reject all three `comic book` → `comics` edits: they corrupt `comic book stores` and `resell ... to comic book stores`, repeating the Episode 111 regression.
Reject `Bobby Brownstar` → `Bobby, porn star`. The speakers explicitly call Bobby Brownstar his first nickname, repeat it throughout, and explain its hygiene-story origin.
Maury Showbizawitz remains a pseudonym because the cast explicitly says they changed his name. Private childhood friends, siblings and partners are not reverse-identified.

Recording awareness is not blanket consent. Bill says he does not want the `little skeleton` used, is pressured until disclosure, later says friends listen and he feels exposed, and refuses a requested demonstration. The record must not call the disclosure wholly voluntary.
Asa's repeated no-lap-dance boundary from Episode 113 continues. She says she has never and would not, repeats no, and rejects every `must happen`, payment and hypothetical workaround.

David explicitly tells fans not to call him `Choey`, says he may refuse photos or autographs, and says accounts may be blocked. Fan familiarity is not permission to override that boundary or send intimate gifts based on Bill's disclosure.

The toy-store customer is a private person. The cast's autism/intellectual-disability labels are unsupported, covert audio lacks permission, and Safeway/cross-street, visit, planted-toy and pen-camera plans must not support identification or contact.

The arson passage remains a literal attributed past account: David says he obtained gasoline after a commercial dispute, while Maury and Harry talked him down and no arson is reported completed. It is not a verified crime or an instruction.

The HIV-through-tears hypothetical is medically wrong. Tears are not an HIV transmission route absent blood contamination; intact skin is an effective barrier, and a generic wound-plus-tears scenario does not establish transmission.
The venue call is evidence of permission-seeking, not final permission. The caller says management has final authority and the episode never records the manager's approval.
Exact hotel room number, elevator/tower directions, keys, transport, schedules, security, private workplaces, cross streets, health, messages, partners and family remain outside public discovery.
The outro's invitation to give Bill underwear is not adopted by the reader: the underlying disclosure followed pressure, and unwanted intimate gifts are not a responsible fan action.

All eleven rejected transformations stay in the fixture so regeneration cannot sanitize ideas, erase pseudonyms, convert recording into blanket consent, or turn private people into investigation targets.
speaker_policy: The recording names recurring cast and public people, but only five coarse embeddings and zero diarized turns exist. These do not pass independently held-out multispeaker validation. Named dialogue remains withheld.

connections.why: Part 02 opens on the same no-gambling and Eva Lin discussion without a narrative reset.
David says past podcasts cannot be taken back and public self-presentation has consequences.
Participants repeatedly check whether audio is active and whether current speech will be used.
The episode proves the phrase is a nickname, not the corrupt `Bobby, porn star` substitution.
The Vegas trip is framed as a live test with friends, security rumors and replacement stimulation.
Asa states she has never given and would not give the requested friend lap dance.
A standing warning is stated, but later topic-specific resistance shows why it is not blanket consent.
Bill says he does not want a private topic used, is pressured, and later reports feeling exposed.
The cast treats a partner's narrow no-breast rule as loopholes instead of seeking affirmative clarity.
The Vegas outcome list again proposes contacting or having sex with Eva without her participation.
The central disclosure explains the later Poon Tees jokes, merchandising pressure and fan-gift outro.
The family pronunciation story explains Christopher → Critifer → Critter.
The cast recites and then explains the long compound name for Bobby.
The speakers explicitly state that they changed the childhood friend's name.
A pressured stop between Las Vegas and Los Angeles produces the Barstow nickname.
